name: Wyckoff Spring (and Upthrust)

card.context: A leader, RS 80 or more, above its 200-day, resting in a sideways range after an advance (a reaccumulation pause). Best when the index itself has just sprung back from a correction. The classic spring after a long decline sits under the 200-day and is off limits.
card.pattern: A flat trading range of 20 sessions or more, 6% to 20% tall, its floor touched by at least two swing lows. The spring day dips 0.1 to 1 ATR under the floor and closes back inside the same day or the next, in the upper half of its range.
card.trigger: PREV LOW RECLAIM: a market order as price trades back above the old range low after a quiet dip, or at the next open after a qualifying close; after a loud dip, wait for the quieter test that holds the spring low.
card.stop: A few cents under the spring low, the lower of the two days on a two-bar spring; the same for the test entry. Over 3%: prefer the test or the intraday reclaim; 3% to 5% at a lower grade; over 5%, skip.
card.failure_mode: The dip keeps going: a close back under the spring low, usually within days and often on a gap. 41% of springs broke their low before any test came and 77% before a close over the range top. A spring that fails usually fails at once.

criteria.statement: Price is above the 200-day SMA on the spring day. No exception: the classic accumulation spring after a long decline is watch only until the stock is back above the line.

options.basis: B26 as written; below-200 springs taught as a read until price is back above (the dossier's rule; the register's default)
a slow terminal shakeout (SPY March 2026, four weeks under the floor, three under the 200-day) bought once back above the 200-day; or sent to the 200-day Remount (setup 13)

criteria.evidence: One-bar springs above the 200-day +0.04R (5,422), below it +0.01R (5,609). MBLY July 2024 (a spring that never sprang, 16% to 50% under the 200-day) and SPY in March 2026 are the cases B26 keeps a long out of. UCT's own springs are leaders in uptrends (DELL 10.5% above its 200-day).

criteria.statement: Preferred: the 60 sessions before the range rose (a reaccumulation pause, Fraser's stepping stone), not a base after a decline.

measure.what: close at the start of the range against the close 60 sessions before it

criteria.evidence: Measured: the prior 60 days up +0.06R against down -0.03R. HWM 2025-08-20 is the stepping-stone case (a range after a 31% run); KMX 2020-12-29 fell 13% into its range and grades lower on this row.

criteria.statement: RS rating 80 or more; stronger than the market through the range.
criteria.evidence: Wyckoff's own strength test: outperforming the market. A spring is not a mean-reversion trade in the house sense, so C31 applies. Measured with an RS proxy: 80 or more +0.05R, a wider stop (3.13%). The RS 80 condition could not be checked on the ten examples.

criteria.statement: Price $10 or more and $20 million a day or more.
criteria.evidence: The dossier's check and the scan used the 20-day average; the glossary's shared window is 50 sessions.

criteria.statement: No new buy within 3 days of a report; skip on buyout news.
criteria.evidence: U 2026-10-29 to 11-02: the right shape in the wrong week; the owner skipped it for earnings and then buyout news. AAPL 2014-04-15 entered 5 sessions before its report, so B22 allowed it, and 3R came on the report gap.

criteria.statement: Springs: a Green or Yellow market. Upthrust shorts: a Red market, below the 200-day.

measure.note: Orange only for an A+; a Red market is for upthrust shorts below the 200-day

criteria.statement: Best when the index itself has just sprung back from a correction (Wyckoff's step 5: time your commitment with a turn in the stock market index).

measure.what: the index's own undercut and reclaim of a prior low
measure.note: a cue; the dossier gives no window

criteria.evidence: Measured by period: 2008-09 -0.34R, 2010-19 +0.18R. AAPL and QQQ 2021-10-01 both sprang on the same day and both made 0.0R: the index's own spring failed, and so did the leader's. UCT's 2025-11 and 2026-04 index notes read the market's own failed breakdowns the same way.

criteria.statement: A sideways trading range of at least 20 sessions behind the spring.

measure.what: sessions in the range before the spring day

options.basis: the app's scanner minimum; the owner's DELL and AMZN ranges were a week or two, sometimes on the hourly (the register's default)
with 3 touches, closer to the classic schematic

criteria.evidence: No source gives a number; support is established in Phases A and B (ChartSchool). The scan used ranges of 60, 40 or 25 sessions (the longest that fits); the ten examples ran 25 to 60. A grade: 4 to 12 weeks.

criteria.statement: A flat floor touched at least twice: two swing lows within about half an ATR of the range low, at least 5 sessions apart. Three or more touches grade higher.

measure.what: swing lows within 0.5 ATR of the range's lowest low, at least 5 sessions apart

criteria.evidence: Borrowed from the app's member drawing (3 touches within 0.5 ATR). Measured: 3 or more touches +0.07R; scan: two touches 27.6% against three or more 26.4% to 3R, no difference. GIS and KMX had four, ODFL five.

criteria.statement: Range height 6% to 20% from the floor to the top. Over 20%: grade lower.
criteria.evidence: Measured: 6% to 10% best (+0.09R, 77% of stops within 3%), 20% to 35% worst (-0.04R, 40% within 3%). TSLA 2025-02-06 (17.9%, near the top of the band, after a 73% run) was stopped on the entry day; its high that day (380.55) was 0.76R over the 373.04 fill, but the same bar took the stop (corrected 2026-11-10 against the bars). A grade: 6% to 12%.

criteria.statement: Flat: no clear slope, the closes drift less than a quarter of the range height.

measure.what: fitted drift of the range's closes / range height

criteria.evidence: The app drawing's rule (the member drawing uses 0.15 of the height, the scan a quarter). MSFT 2020-09-18 was dropped on sight: an 18% range that slopes with the high at the end is not flat. The flat base card measures flat as 10% of the average close; the two cards' lookalike lines say which applies.

criteria.statement: The spring: the day's low goes under the range's lowest low by at least 0.1 ATR (a real undercut) and at most about 1 ATR. Over 1 ATR is a shakeout (grade lower); over 2 ATR is a breakdown, not a spring.

measure.note: 1 to 2 ATR grades lower; over 2 ATR is not a spring

criteria.evidence: Shallow is Fraser's #3 spring; the numbers are the dossier's. Measured: a dip under 0.5 ATR +0.04R with 23.1% to 3R; 1 to 2 ATR +0.02R, 12.8% to 3R, a 5.01% median stop. Scan: 0.1 to 0.5 ATR 27.5% against 0.5 to 1.0 ATR 26.0%. The ten examples dipped 0.13 to 0.80 ATR.

criteria.statement: The reclaim: it closes back above the old range low the same day (one-bar), or the next day (two-bar). Later than that: not this setup.

measure.what: sessions from the spring day to the first close back above the range low

options.basis: count two-bar springs (they measured better, +0.15R; the owner's AMZN example; the dossier and the register's default)
one-bar only (ChartSchool's close within the TR)

criteria.evidence: ChartSchool: reverses to close within the TR; the glossary's 1-3 days. Measured: one-bar +0.03R (11,031), two-bar +0.15R (3,898); scan: one-bar 27.2% against two-bar 26.0% to 3R. The app's pattern-engine scanner cannot see a one-bar spring at all (conflicts). The shared reclaim window is 3 sessions; this card keeps the Wyckoff reading of 2.

criteria.statement: Close quality: the reclaim day closes in the upper half of its range.

measure.what: (close - low) / (high - low) of the reclaim day

criteria.evidence: Measured: a close in the top 30% of the day +0.06R (+0.01 to +0.12). A grade: the top third, then a strong up day on more volume (an SOS).

criteria.statement: Record the dip's volume against the 50-day average. Quiet (under 1.0x): the reclaim can be bought. Loud (1.5x or more): wait for the test. Not a pass or fail gate.

measure.note: 1.5x or more sends the entry to the test

options.basis: use it to choose the entry: quiet = buy now, loud = wait for the test (Fraser, Pruden; the dossier)
a grading cue only (the register's default for every setup)
ignore it (the daily data showed no difference either way)

criteria.evidence: The single biggest disagreement among the sources: the Wyckoff school wants a quiet spring and a test after a loud one; Taylor (CMT) wants heavy volume, the higher the better. Measured on daily bars: quiet (under 0.8x) +0.02R, 0.8x to 1.5x +0.04R, 1.5x or more +0.01R, 2.5x or more +0.05R; no separation. The ten examples dipped on 0.81x to 1.16x.

criteria.statement: Often the spring undercuts the 20-day or 50-day too (the owner's shakeout below the 20EMA and remount; shakeout under the 50SMA). It must stay above the 200-day.

measure.what: spring-day low against the 20-day EMA or 50-day SMA
measure.note: a cue; the close stays above the 200-day

criteria.evidence: BTC 2025-07-27 and GLW 2026-06-21 in the owner's notes; BE 2026-06-21: after getting stopped below the 50SMA (dirty shakeout) but leaders do that sometimes.

criteria.statement: Option A, the reclaim: a market order as price trades back above the old range low after the dip (intraday, the owner's DELL plan, reclaim of $142), or at the next open after a qualifying close. For quiet springs where the stop fits A13.

measure.what: intraday price after the dip, or the next open

options.basis: the reclaim (the owner's DELL plan; Fraser's #3 spring)
both, by volume: quiet = the reclaim, loud = the test (the dossier's recommendation)
also the back-up after the range top (the LPS or BUEC)

criteria.evidence: The owner's DELL math (2026-03-08): shakeout to $140 and reclaim of $142, so entry $142, stop $140, 3-1 by the time the breakout buyers step in. Measured: the spring itself at the next open +0.06R; the owner's intraday plan on DELL risked 3.2% against 5.6% at the next open and saw 10.5R within 20 sessions. The register's default for every daily setup is the trade-through at market.

criteria.statement: Option B, the test: 1 to 10 sessions after a loud spring, a quieter dip back toward the old floor that holds above the spring low and closes in its upper half; buy at the next open (or on its intraday turn), stop under the spring low.

measure.what: sessions from the spring to the test bar
measure.and: the test holds above the spring low, on lower volume, and closes in its upper half

criteria.evidence: Measured on the same springs: the test entry +0.11R (+0.14R above the 200-day) against +0.06R for the immediate entry; a test was found after 36% of springs, and 41% broke the spring low before any test came, so waiting skips those. ODFL 2021-10-01 is the kind the test entry would also have caught.

criteria.statement: Option C, the back-up (LPS or BUEC): after the push to the top of the range, the first light-volume pullback that holds the old top. The add or the second chance; it overlaps the flat-base breakout.
Not the breakout over the range top with the stop under the spring low (the app's scanner plan): a median 12.5% stop and 1% reached 3R.

measure.what: median stop of the range-top breakout entry with the stop under the spring low

criteria.evidence: Pruden and von Lichtenstein: you should not buy breakouts. Measured: only 16% of springs reached the range top first, 77% broke the spring low first; the entry +0.01R with no stop within 3%. The same breakout with the stop under the breakout day's low (the house default) is the Flat Base card's trade, -0.02R here.

criteria.statement: No chase: skip if the entry is more than 4% above the old range low, the buy point.

options.basis: the old range low (the dossier's proposal; the register's default names the trigger level)

criteria.evidence: The scan skipped any entry more than 4% past the floor; a next open back under the floor filled at the floor when price traded through it that day.

criteria.statement: At entry, no more than 10% above the 10-day average.
criteria.evidence: Rarely binding: a spring happens at the bottom of a range.

criteria.statement: A few cents under the spring low (for a two-bar spring the lower of the two days). The same for the test entry.

measure.value: a few cents under the lowest low of the dip

criteria.evidence: Fraser: under the low of the Spring day. Taylor: the spring low should not be violated by any significant degree. Not the old range low (too tight; the spring low is the real line), and not the app's 1.5% under it with a breakout entry (a median 14.3% stop in the replay of the app's code).

criteria.statement: Size from the stop (A5). If it is more than about 3% away: prefer the test or the intraday reclaim to tighten it; 3% to 5% only at a lower grade (smaller risk, E49); over 5%, skip.

measure.note: about 3% at full grade; 3% to 5% graded down

options.basis: skip over 3% (A13 read as a cap)
allow 3% to 5% at a lower grade (the dossier's proposal)
allow anything with the size cut by A5 (the register's default: up to one ADR, one grade lower)

criteria.evidence: A13 is the main friction. Measured: 62% of one-bar springs had the stop within 3% at the next open (median 2.27%); deeper dips and tall ranges push it past. Scan: stop under 3% 27.1% / 18.5% to 3R / 5R, 3% to 5% 27.1% / 15.1%. The owner's examples at the next open ran 3.3% to 6.3% (AMZN 3.3%, LHX 3.6%, DELL 5.6%, BE 6.3%); his own intraday plans were 1.4% (DELL) and 2.3% (AMZN).

criteria.statement: Never lower it; a real stop order with the broker.
A gap through the stop: the first 30-minute low is the new stop; out if past 2R.

measure.what: loss at the first 30-minute low of the gap-down day

criteria.evidence: A failed spring often gaps down (HPE, October 2026; AMZN 2026-09-01 gapped through the stop for -1.02R). The upthrust short NVO 2025-12-12 gapped from 48.10 to 52.67 through a 50.78 stop.

criteria.statement: A third at 3R.
Breakeven between 2R and 5R, at the first trim by default.

measure.what: R at which the stop moves to the entry

criteria.statement: A third at 5R.
If it opens above a trim level, take that trim at the open.
Trail the rest under the 21-day (most springs) or the 10-day (fast movers), out on a close below it.

measure.what: close against the 21-day (most springs) or 10-day (fast) average

criteria.evidence: The dossier's check trailed the last third on a close through the 21-day EMA after 5R; DELL 2026-03-10 trailed out after 79 sessions for +12.8R.

criteria.statement: The top of the range is the first resistance. From the reclaim entry it sat a median 4.8R away (72% of the time 3R or more), so the 3R trim usually comes at or before the range top.
criteria.evidence: The owner's DELL note says the same: 3-1 by the time the breakout buyers step in. A grade: the range top 4R or more away; B-: under 3R to the range top.

criteria.statement: The Wyckoff point-and-figure count may be shown as a stop, look and listen level, not taught as a rule.
criteria.evidence: Wyckoff targets come from the P&F count (ChartSchool, Pruden, Fraser). The app's target of twice the range height is in no source.

criteria.statement: Under 1R after 10 sessions: out.
criteria.evidence: Fits a spring that stalls: the sources' advice is to wait for a new spring or test, which C33 turns into an exit.

criteria.statement: Before the buy: no real range behind the dip. A falling stock makes a new low every day; that is not a spring.
criteria.evidence: The base catalog's own comment. IREN 2025-10-22 (191% above its 200-day, ATR 14%) was a pullback in a vertical stock, not a range spring; the next 20 sessions -33%.

criteria.statement: Before the buy: a close back under the spring low, or a dip that keeps going (over 2 ATR) on heavy volume (Fraser's #1 spring, which should not be bought).

measure.or: a close back under the spring low before the entry

criteria.evidence: Fraser: a Shakeout (#1 Spring) is a failed Spring that should not be bought. HPE's hoped-for shakeout under $60 in October 2026 became a breakdown to 43.38.

criteria.statement: After the buy: the stop under the spring low is the exit. A spring that fails usually fails at once: 41% broke their low before any test came, 77% before a close over the range top.

measure.what: share of springs that broke the spring low before a close over the range top

criteria.evidence: MSFT 2023-08-08: everything the rules ask for, stopped on the entry day (2023-08-09); the day's high (327.11) was 0.18R over the 326.47 fill, but the same bar took the stop (corrected 2026-11-10 against the bars). The stop is the trade, not a formality. The register's D-136: no setup adds an exit before the stop.

a_plus: spr.prior_advance: above a rising 50-day and 200-day after a prior advance
spr.leader: RS 90 or more, a leader in a leading group; held up while the market fell
spr.range_length: 4 to 12 weeks, flat, 6% to 12% tall (spr.range_height), 3 or more clean touches of the floor (spr.floor_touches)
spr.volume: shrinking on the down swings inside the range; quiet on the dip, or loud followed by a quiet test that holds
spr.dip_depth: shallow (under about 0.5 ATR), late in the range
spr.reclaim_close: closes in the top third, then a strong up day on more volume (an SOS)
spr.range_top_resistance: the range top 4R or more away
spr.index_sprung: Green; the index itself just sprang back (spr.market_reading)
b_minus: spr.above_200: barely above the 200-day; a flat or falling 50-day
spr.leader: RS 80 to 85; the group lagging
spr.range_length: short, sloppy or tall (over 20%, spr.range_height), only 2 touches (spr.floor_touches)
spr.volume: heavy on the down swings; loud on the dip with no test yet
spr.dip_depth: deep (over 1 ATR), or early in the range
spr.reclaim_close: a weak close, no follow-through
spr.range_top_resistance: under 3R to the range top
no_trade: spr.inv_close_under_low: a close back under the spring low, or a dip over 2 ATR on heavy volume
spr.inv_no_range: no real range behind the dip
spr.reclaim_window: no close back inside the range by the next day
spr.earnings_window: earnings within 3 days, or buyout news
spr.not_breakout_entry: the range-top breakout with the stop under the spring low
spr.no_chase: more than 4% above the old range low
spr.market_reading: an upthrust short above the 200-day; a spring in a Red market

lookalikes.tell: Look left. A spring needs a flat range of 20 sessions or more (15 on the app's minimum) with a floor touched at least twice, and the close back inside the same day or the next; a U&R's level can be one swing low, a rising average or a prior high, and it may take 3 sessions to close back above.

Count the touches. A 2B's level is one swing low with a rally of at least 1 ATR between the low and the break; a spring's floor is a flat level touched by two or more swing lows at least 5 sessions apart inside a sideways range.

Where does the trade start? A flat base is bought through the TOP of the range with the stop under the breakout day's low; a spring is bought at the FLOOR on the reclaim after the undercut, with the stop under the dip and the range top a median 4.8R away. A flat base is flat when its closes drift under 10% of price; a Wyckoff range when they drift under a quarter of its height.
Count the closes under the floor. A spring is back inside within 2 sessions (one-bar or two-bar); 5 or more closes under the level is a Remount of a level, bought on the retake.
Which low broke? An Oops breaks yesterday's low and reclaims yesterday's close on one candle; a spring breaks the floor of a range of 20 sessions or more that was touched at least twice.

Measure the dip. A spring goes 0.1 to 1 ATR under the floor in a stock above its 200-day; over 2 ATR is a breakdown, and a 2 ATR flush on 2x volume under the fast averages with the burst boxes checked is a capitulation, which may sit under the 200-day as a parabolic long.

invalidations: Before the buy: no real range behind the dip (spr.inv_no_range).
Before the buy: a close back under the spring low, or a dip over 2 ATR on heavy volume (spr.inv_close_under_low).
Before the buy: no close back inside the range by the next day (spr.reclaim_window).
Before the buy: below the 200-day (spr.above_200); earnings within 3 days or buyout news (spr.earnings_window).
After the buy: the stop under the spring low (spr.after_entry_stop).
After the buy: under 1R after 10 sessions, out (spr.time_stop).
mistakes: Buying a breakdown that never closed back inside the range.
Calling any undercut a spring when there is no flat range behind it.
Buying a loud, deep dip at once instead of waiting for the quieter test (Fraser).
Putting the stop under the old range low (too tight; the spring low is the real line) or far below it.
Buying the range-top breakout and keeping the stop under the spring low (the app's plan): a 12.5% median stop.
Buying a spring under the 200-day after a long decline (B26).
Shorting an upthrust in a leader above the 200-day (B26; UCT; measured -0.16R).
Adding to, or averaging down on, a spring that broke its low (A5, A4).
Chasing the reclaim more than 4% above the old low (C28).

short_mirror.note: The upthrust, dossier 8.6: only below the 200-day SMA, RS 20 or less, in a weak group (B26, the C31 mirror); the same range rules mirrored at the ceiling; the day's high goes over the range's highest high by 0.1 to 1 ATR and the day closes back inside, or closes back inside the next day; short at the next open, better on the failed retest of the upthrust high (Fraser: the test of the UTAD is a strategic place for short sellers); stop a few cents over the upthrust high; skip hard-to-borrow (D48); grade cap B until the owner rules. Measured: the upthrust short lost -0.13R overall and -0.16R above the 200-day where B26 forbids it; in the house-legal zone +0.09R (range -0.06 to +0.23). The scan's shorts below the 200-day: 22.0% to 3R (GS 2018-11-08, TGT 2023-07-27). Not a short in a leader above the 200-day: UCT reads that as a coming failed breakout-squat buy. The more useful lesson is the warning for longs: a breakout that closes back inside its range is a reason not to buy, or to sell a position bought on it. Whether to teach the short, the warning only, or drop it is D-001 (35:8).

best_conditions: Springs: a Green or Yellow market (F65), best when the index itself has just sprung back from a correction (Wyckoff's step 5; UCT's 2025-11 and 2026-04 index notes). Measured: bad in 2008-09 (-0.34R), best in 2010-19 (+0.18R). Upthrust shorts: a Red market, below the 200-day (D46); measured best in 2008-09 (+0.14R).

management.trail: a close under the 21-day for most springs, the 10-day for a fast mover (E52)
management.breakeven: between 2R and 5R, at the first trim by default (B19)
management.gap_open: a trim level the day opens past is taken at the open (F63)
management.gap_against: the first 30-minute low is the new stop; out if past 2R (B20)
management.overrides: none. The dossier (8.4) keeps the house defaults and adds a note: the range top is the first resistance, a median 4.8R from the reclaim entry, so the 3R trim usually comes at or before it; the P&F count may be shown as a level, not a rule. Not ours: the app's target of twice the range height.

base_rate.window: 60 sessions forward, fixed stop 3 cents beyond the probe's extreme, skipped when wider than 5%, no trims, no breakeven, no trail; 2000-01 to 2026-11; the fill at the next open (or at the floor when the open was back under it); a range of 60, 40 or 25 sessions, 6% to 20% tall, drift under a quarter of the height, two floor touches; one hit per name per 30 sessions

dossier_check_section_4_3.note: house plan, 1996 to 2026; a small edge at best, about 0.1R better than a random entry with the same plan

uct_named: DELL 2026-03-10 (the owner's model trade, +12.8R at the next open; his plan: entry 142, stop 137.47)
AMZN 2026-08-27/28 (a two-bar spring, gapped through the stop on 09-01, -1.02R)
U 2026-10-29 to 11-02 (the right shape, B22 forbids it)
MBLY July 2024 (Bracco: a spring that never sprang; B26)
QQQ 2025-12-10 (Bracco: a UTAD; B26 forbids the short)

failures.why: a 25-day range 373.04 to 439.74, 17.9% tall, three touches, probe 0.52 ATR on 0.97x volume, stop 2.65%; bought 373.04 (the floor; the entry-day open, 370.19, was under it); the entry day's high (380.55) was 0.76R over the fill, but the same bar's low (360.34) took the 363.15 stop first, so the best is 0.0R (corrected 2026-11-10 against the bars): the earlier text said it never traded above the entry. It broke the spring low on the entry day and gapped on. A tall range after a 73% run in the prior 60 sessions, in a market turning down.

a 40-day range, 13.1% tall, three touches, a cents-deep 0.16 ATR probe on 0.76x volume, stop 1.07%: everything the rules ask for, stopped on the entry day (2023-08-09); the day's high (327.11) was 0.64, or 0.18R, over the 326.47 fill, but the same bar's low (321.05) took the 322.97 stop first (corrected 2026-11-10 against the bars): the earlier text said it never showed a profit and was stopped on the third day. A spring that fails usually fails at once.
AAPL and QQQ both sprang on the same day and both made 0.0R: a market-wide shakeout that did not finish; the index's own spring failed, and so did the leader's.

an upthrust short, stop 1.64%; ran to 2.98R, a hair short of the 3R trim, then gapped from 48.10 to an open of 52.67 through the 50.78 stop on 12-23. B20 applies; the upthrust short below the 200-day stays capped at grade B.

a 40-day range 57.92-64.85 (12.0% tall, two touches), a 0.14 ATR probe on 0.91x volume, closed back inside the same day; bought 58.44 at the 05-10 open, stop 57.70 (1.27%); that day dipped to 57.32 through the stop and the stock fell to 51.35 by 06-03 as SPY made lower lows (279.93 on 05-13). Not a Green market.

examples.limits: Daily bars only (the owner's intraday reclaim and B20 cannot be tested; the next-open entry is usually worse than the reclaim); the range and spring rules are one reading of sources that publish no numbers; no RS rating or group (C31 not applied); survivors; events cluster on market-wide days; one management plan; no commissions, slippage, borrow fees. Nothing here is a published statistic, and no published success rate for springs exists.

near_misses.why: the probe went 1.34 ATR under the 359.50 floor (to 352.44), one close under, back inside the next day; the rule is 0.1 to 1 ATR (1 to 2 ATR grades lower, over 2 is a breakdown). Stop 2.46%; made 0.52R, stopped.

3 closes under the 25.61 floor and the close back inside on day 4; the rule is the same day or the next. A U&R of the range low at best (29-undercut-rally), with more closes a Remount; made 0.35R, stopped.

the floor (164.99) was touched by one swing low, 40 sessions old, that price rallied 14% off; the rule is a flat floor touched at least twice. A 2B of a single low (28-2b-reversal), not a spring; made 0.01R, stopped.
the range behind the probe is 19 sessions long (118.24-126.71 from 08-18); the rule is 20 or more. A U&R of a three-week shelf low (29-undercut-rally), not a spring; made 0.87R, stopped.

question_seeds.seed: A one-bar spring and a two-bar spring: what is the difference, and by when must the close be back inside the range?
Where does the stop go on a spring: under the old range low, or under the spring low?
